author: Jason Stys
summary: Resolve base/local/server conflicts using explicit choices for divergent fields, stale-version checks and atomic replacement of queued writes.
rationale: Makes offline editing recoverable without silently overwriting another person's changes or fabricating a missing base.
limitations: Isolated synthetic development API with no authentication or tenant separation; not a hosted multi-user field service.
Local SQLite is unencrypted. Older drafts may lack a base revision, which the resolver does not fabricate.
Conflict review shows at most 100 entries from a 200-item bounded store API.
MAUI compilation and portable view-model journeys are not real-device GUI validation; no updated native release accompanies this upgrade.

visualReview.method: Every rendered page individually viewed at readable original resolution

scope: Reviewed documentation editions of the cited source. Checksums identify bytes, not authorship. Historical measurements retain their own dates; integration CI must be checked separately.
